_comment: scripts/build_installer.ps1 and tests/test_installer.py -- there is no second copy.
'sha256' and 'authenticode_subject' are TRUST ANCHORS. They are established once,
deliberately, by running the prepare script with -Pin against the official URL, and are
never edited to make a failing verification pass. A mismatch means the file is not the
one that was reviewed; the correct response is to investigate, not to update the value.
The Authenticode signature is the stronger of the two: the checksum only proves the file
is byte-identical to the one that was pinned, whereas the signature proves EDB published
it, independently of how it was obtained. Both are checked.
To move to a new PostgreSQL version: change 'version', 'major', 'filename' and 'url',
set 'sha256' to null, re-run the prepare script with -Pin, and record the new value.

postgresql.authenticode_subject: CN=EnterpriseDB Corporation, O=EnterpriseDB Corporation, S=Massachusetts, C=US
postgresql.publisher: EDB (the official PostgreSQL Windows installer linked from postgresql.org)
notes: PostgreSQL 16 is a supported major version (community support to November 2028) and
matches the major version this project has been developed and tested against.
The installer is BitRock/InstallBuilder based; its unattended options are documented
and assembled in app/postgres_install.py, which builds the command line.
